visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) A close-up shot shows a person's hands forcibly stuffing a sesame-seeded hamburger into a white plastic mooncake mold. The background is a textured light-colored surface. (2) In a vertical split-screen, the top half shows the hand pressing the mold down while the bottom half introduces a young man wearing glasses and a black t-shirt looking at his phone with a curious expression. (3) The top frame shows the mold being lifted to reveal the burger now shaped like a traditional round mooncake with an intricate decorative pattern on top. The man below watches intently. (4) The video transitions to a single frame showing the hands placing a different burger onto a white ceramic plate and pressing a hexagonal white mold over it. (5) The hexagonal mold is pressed firmly against the plate with both hands to compress the food. (6) The mold is lifted, revealing the burger has taken the shape of a hexagonal mooncake with a complex floral crest on the surface. (7) A close-up shot focuses on the details of the hexagonal 'burger mooncake' on the white plate. (8) The young man appears full-screen in a well-lit indoor room, holding the hexagonal burger mooncake and taking a large bite. His facial expression shows surprise as he chews.

audio_base.audio_narrative_log: (1) A bouncy, high-pitched recorder melody starts with a fast tempo, establishing a playful and comedic atmosphere. No vocals are present initially. (2) A male voice interjects with a sharp, high-arousal exclamation '真的假的', featuring a dramatic rising pitch contour that signals extreme surprise and skepticism. (3) The rhythmic recorder BGM continues with a bright, percussive woodblock-like sound underpinning the melody. (4) The audio concludes with a prominent, dry crunching sound, representing a bite into food, while the playful music continues at a steady volume before a hard cut at the end.

narrative_and_purpose.mainPurpose: To entertain the audience by demonstrating a quirky food hack that turns ordinary burgers into mooncake shapes, validating the humorous philosophical premise that a 'mooncake' is defined only by its physical form rather than its ingredients.
